tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and compliance with the visual spec. Hygroscopicity: glass weighing vessel, weigh vessel+stopper (m1); add about 2 g and weigh (m2); stand un-stoppered in climatic cabinet at 25 +/- 1 C for 24 h; stopper and weigh (m3); calculate % increase in mass.

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility); BP Monograph for Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:30

tests.procedure: Stepwise solubility: 100 mg powdered sample in stoppered tube, add 0.1 mL solvent, shake vigorously 1 min, hold at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C for 15 min (repeat shake+hold once if not dissolved); if not dissolved add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL with the same shake/hold; then 10 mg + 10 mL, then 1 mg + 10 mL; classify very soluble ... practically insoluble. Repeat with methylene chloride.

solvents: water (implied by spec; not named in STM)
details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section; BP Monograph for Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:31

tests.procedure: pH, described under the pH test (6.5).
tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:32

tests.procedure: Prepare, with shaking and without heating, a mixture of 4.0 g sample and 20 mL carbon dioxide-free water (appears as a gel). Add 100 mL carbon dioxide-free water. Shake. A suspension forms that settles after standing. The suspension is used for Solution S1.

details.intermediateObservation: mixture has the appearance of a gel

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:32

tests.procedure: To an acidified solution add iodinated potassium iodide solution R1. The solution becomes blue or violet.

details.reagent: Potassium Iodide Solution, Iodinated R1 (500 mg iodine + 1.5 g potassium iodide in water to 25 mL)

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:32

tests.procedure: To 2 mL of Solution S2 add 2 mL of a 150 g/L potassium carbonate solution; heat to boiling (no precipitate forms). Add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution; heat to boiling; cool in iced water. A dense white precipitate is formed.

details.intermediate: no precipitate after carbonate and boiling
details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Sodium

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:32

tests.procedure: Compare 2 mL of Solution S1 with 2 mL of purified water for clarity and colour.

details.solutionS1: supernatant after centrifuging the suspension from identification test B at 2500 g for 10 min
details.reference: BP Appendix IV B Color of Solution, IV A Clarity of Solution

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:33,28

tests.procedure: Disperse 1.0 g in 30 mL carbon dioxide-free water; measure with a calibrated pH meter.

details.reference: BP Appendix V L. Determination of pH Values

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:34

tests.procedure: Limit test by colour comparison. Sample: 10 mL of Solution S2 + 2 mL of 200 g/L citric acid monohydrate + 0.1 mL thioglycolic acid; mix; make alkaline with ammonia; dilute to 20 mL with water. Standard: 10 mL iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe) treated identically. After 5 min any pink colour in the test solution is not more intense than in the standard.

details.citricAcidSolution: 2 mL of 200 g/L citric acid monohydrate
details.standardSolution: 10 mL iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe)
details.solutionS2: 2.5 g in silica or platinum crucible + 2 mL of 500 g/L sulfuric acid; heat on water-bath, then cautiously over naked flame raising temperature progressively; incinerate in muffle furnace at 600 +/- 25 C until black particles disappear; cool, add few drops dilute sulfuric acid, heat and incinerate again; cool, add few drops ammonium carbonate solution, evaporate to dryness, incinerate cautiously; cool and dissolve residue in 50 mL water
details.ironStd20ppm: dilute to 10 times its volume with water a solution containing ferric ammonium sulfate equivalent to 0.863 g and 25 mL dilute sulfuric acid in 500.0 mL
details.ironStd1ppm: dilute iron standard solution (20 ppm Fe) to 20 times its volume with water
details.ammoniumCarbonateSolution: 15.8 g ammonium carbonate in water to 100 mL
details.diluteSulfuricAcid: 5.5 mL sulfuric acid + 60 mL water, cool, dilute to 100 mL
details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Iron

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:35,28

tests.procedure: Weighing bottle previously dried at 130 C, cooled in desiccator (W0). Weigh accurately 1.000 g into it (W1 = empty bottle + material). Dry in calibrated oven at 130 C for 1.5 h; cool in desiccator; weigh (W2). Repeat drying until constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: BP Appendix IX D. Determination of Loss on Drying

tests.source: Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A__STM Sodium Starch Glycolate Type A.txt:36

tests.procedure: 70 mL water in a flask; add 1.0 g sample (dried substance); stir with glass rod until no lumps; transfer to 100 mL graduated cylinder; rinse flask walls with water; dilute to 100 mL; stir until evenly distributed; stand 4 h; read sediment volume.
